units: Y. Kidd. III, 64ᶜ bot. מהו ממזר מום זר what is mamzer (מַמְזֵר)? Something repulsive; Yeb. 76ᵇ ממזר כתיב מ׳ זר the Law says mamzer which means anything repulsive (male or female); Sifré Deut. 248 כל שהוא מומזר (corr. acc.) whatever is in any way repulsive.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 5:5">Bekh. V, 5</cite>, a. fr. <he>בעל מ׳</he> having a blemish (unfit for the altar, for priestly service &c.).
<cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 6:9">Ib. VI, 9</cite>, a. fr. <he>הרי זה מ׳</he> this is a legal blemish; <he>אינה מ׳</he> this is not &c.—
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 59b:15">B. Mets. 59ᵇ</cite> <he>מ׳ שבך וכ׳</he> do not reproach thy neighbor with a fault which is also thine own; a. fr.—Pl. <he>מוּמִין</he>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 6:1">Bekh. VI, 1</cite> <he>על אלו מ׳ וכ׳</he> these are the blemishes in consequence of which a first-born animal may be slaughtered (after the destruction of the Temple).
<cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 6:2">Ib. 2</cite> <he>אין מ׳ בלבן</he> a blemish in the white of the eye is no blemish in the sense of the law.
Ib. VII, 1 מ׳ אלו … פוסלין וכ׳ the above named blemishes, whether permanent or transitory, make also human beings unfit (for priesthood &c.); a. fr.—Denom. הוּמָם to become blemished, defective.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 4:4:5">Y. Shek. IV, 48ᵇ</cite> <he>שפודין תמימין והוּמְמוּ</he> they had redeemed them when they were without blemish, and they became blemished.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 12:8">Num. R. s. 12</cite>, end; <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 6:4:2">Cant. R. to VI, 4</cite> <he>ולא הוממו וכ׳</he> and they have not become unfit for sacrifices on account of blemishes or old age &c., v. <cite ref="G00102"><he>זָהַם</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 2:2:3">Y. Yoma II, 39ᵈ</cite> <he>קטורת שכבת הוּמָמָה</he> frankincense which was extinguished is unfit for the altar.
